I am a conservation biologist with over a decade of field and academic
experience, currently a research associate at the
[University of Rome Tor Vergata](https://www.uniroma2.it). My work is driven by
curiosity about evolutionary processes and ecological resilience in island
systems, which has led me to study some of the rarest and most critically
endangered 🦎 on Earth, from the Turks and Caicos to the Bahamas and the
Galapagos.

That intellectual drive is matched by a deep empathy for the species I work to
protect, their environment, and the local communities who share their
existence. I approach conservation not as an outsider but as a collaborator,
listening to local knowledge and integrating it into scientifically rigorous
frameworks. Whether leading field crews in remote locations or co-developing
proposals with interdisciplinary colleagues, I believe trust, respect, and
shared purpose are the foundation of successful conservation.

This site is where I keep track of my [research](research.qmd),
[publications](publications.qmd), and ideas. Have a look at my
[now page](now.qmd) for what I am working on at the moment, the
[blog](blog.qmd) for longer thoughts, or the [photos](photos.qmd) I bring back
from the field. Welcome and I hope you find something interesting.
